whatIs.title: 1. What is WinStack
whatIs.description: WinStack is a simple, accessible web store that uses the official WinGet (Windows Package Manager) catalog to install applications on Windows 10 and 11.
whatIs.point1: Pick apps visually without memorizing package names.
whatIs.point2: We generate a native WinStack installer (.cmd) that opens a clean progress window and installs everything automatically — no PowerShell setup required.
whatIs.point3: Free, bilingual (PT/EN), and designed for quick setups.

downloadRun.title: 2. How to download and run the installer
downloadRun.intro: After building your stack in the store, follow these steps to deploy your apps:
downloadRun.step1: Open the sidebar stack and confirm all desired apps are listed.
downloadRun.step2: Click download installer to save winstack-install.cmd to your computer.
downloadRun.step3: Open your Downloads folder and double-click winstack-install.cmd.
downloadRun.step4: If Windows asks for administrator permission (UAC), click Yes — required to install software.
downloadRun.step5: Wait for the WinStack installer terminal window to open and install everything automatically.

motw.title: 3. PowerShell execution policy (does not apply to .cmd)
motw.intro: The .cmd installer bypasses PowerShell execution policy automatically. If you copy the .ps1 script manually (Advanced mode), you may see "script is not digitally signed".
motw.step1: Always prefer the winstack-install.cmd file from the site — just double-click it.
motw.step2: The .cmd requests administrator permission when needed and runs PowerShell with execution policy bypass.
motw.step3: If you still run the .ps1 directly, open PowerShell and run: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\winstack-install.ps1
motw.step5: For scripts downloaded from the internet, Windows may also apply Mark-of-the-Web — see below.
motw.tip: Tip: the .cmd installer automatically unblocks (MOTW) the embedded script.

installWinget.title: 4. How to install WinGet (App Installer)
installWinget.description: WinGet ships with Microsoft's App Installer. If the winget command does not work in PowerShell, install or update App Installer:
installWinget.step1: Open the Microsoft Store using the link below or search for App Installer.
installWinget.step2: Click Get or Update and wait for the installation to finish.
installWinget.storeLinkLabel: Open App Installer in Microsoft Store
installWinget.note: After installing, close and reopen PowerShell. Type winget --version to confirm it is working.

notepad.title: 5. Alternative: copy script to Notepad
notepad.intro: If Windows blocks the downloaded file, you can create the script manually and avoid Mark-of-the-Web:
notepad.step1: In the sidebar list, use the Copy script button to copy the content.
notepad.step2: Open Notepad from the Start menu.
notepad.step4: Go to File → Save As, pick a folder, and save as InstallApps.ps1 (type: All files).
notepad.step5: Run the saved file in PowerShell as administrator — no unblock step needed.

about.metaDescription: What WinStack is, why we built it, and how it helps you set up a fresh Windows from the official WinGet catalog.
about.title: About WinStack
about.intro: WinStack started from a simple wish: to make setting up a fresh Windows less tedious and a little more human. We're an indie, open-source project with no profit motive.

what.title: What it is
what.body: WinStack is a web store that brings together the official WinGet catalog, Microsoft's package manager. Instead of hunting for installers all over the web, you find everything in one place, with a calm interface that's easy to browse.

why.title: Why it exists
why.body: We've all spent an afternoon reinstalling Windows, downloading program after program, site after site. We figured it could be better. WinStack exists so you can go from a blank machine to your favorite setup in a few clicks, without memorizing commands.

how.title: How it works
how.body: The idea is straightforward, in three steps:
how.step1: Discover apps by browsing the catalog and our ready-made kits.
how.step2: Build your stack by gathering everything you want to install.
how.step3: Generate and download an install script that handles the rest, using WinGet under the hood.

openSource.title: Open and non-profit
openSource.body: WinStack is open-source and not-for-profit. We don't sell anything, we don't show ads, and the code is out in the open for anyone to read, audit, or contribute to. It's a project made by people who love software, for people who love software.

cta.title: Ready to start?
cta.description: Browse the catalog and build your first stack.

privacy.metaDescription: How WinStack handles your data: anonymous authentication, what we store, and why there's no third-party tracking.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: We'd rather be straight with you: WinStack collects as little as possible and never sells your data. Here's everything that happens to your information, in plain words.

anonymous.title: Anonymous authentication
anonymous.body: You don't need to create an account, give an email, or set a password. We create an automatic anonymous identity for you, just so your favorites and stacks stick around between visits. No personal data is required.

stored.title: What we store
stored.body: Tied to your anonymous identity, we only keep:
stored.item1: The apps you've marked as favorites.
stored.item2: The stacks and bundles you've built and saved.
stored.item3: The history of install scripts you've generated.

noTracking.title: No third-party tracking
noTracking.body: We don't use advertising trackers or social pixels, and we don't resell data. There are no ads on WinStack. What you do here stays here.

catalog.title: Where the catalog comes from
catalog.body: App information comes from the official, public WinGet catalog, maintained by the community and Microsoft. We simply organize and present that data to make your choices easier.

cta.title: All set on privacy
cta.description: Whenever you like, head back and build your stack.

terms.metaDescription: WinStack's terms of use: using the tool, no warranties, and your responsibility when running scripts.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms explain, without unnecessary legalese, the rules for using WinStack. By using the tool, you agree to them.

use.title: Using the tool
use.body: WinStack is offered free of charge to help you discover apps and generate install scripts via WinGet. You're free to use it for personal and professional purposes, as long as you do so legally and responsibly.

asIs.title: No warranties
asIs.body: WinStack is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind. We do our best to keep everything working, but we can't guarantee the service will always be available, error-free, or fit for a particular purpose.

responsibility.title: Your responsibility
responsibility.body: The scripts you generate run on your own computer, with your own permissions. You're responsible for reviewing what you install and for running the scripts. We recommend checking the apps you've picked — advanced mode shows the commands before you download.

thirdParty.title: Third-party apps
thirdParty.body: The apps in the catalog are created and maintained by third parties and distributed under their own licenses and terms. WinStack doesn't develop these apps and isn't responsible for them; it only makes installing them from the WinGet catalog easier.

faq.metaDescription: Answers to the most common questions about WinStack: whether it's free, whether you need an account, script safety, and compatibility.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: We've gathered the questions that come up most. If yours isn't here, take a look at the Help Center.

items.q1: Do I need to be a computer administrator?
items.a1: In most cases, yes. The installer automatically requests administrator permission (UAC prompt) when you are not already elevated.
items.a2: The script only installs packages you chose in the store, using Microsoft's official winget command. You can review the content in Advanced mode before downloading.
items.a3: Yes, as long as WinGet (App Installer) is installed and up to date. Windows 11 includes WinGet by default; on Windows 10 you may need to install it from the Microsoft Store.
items.q4: What if an app fails to install?
items.a4: The script continues installing the remaining apps. Check your internet connection, whether the app is available in your region, and disk space. You can try installing the app individually later with winget install PackageName.
items.a5: Yes, completely. WinStack is an open-source, not-for-profit project — we charge nothing, have no paid tiers, and show no ads.
items.q6: Do I need to create an account?
items.a6: No. You use WinStack with an anonymous identity created automatically, with no email or password. It only exists to keep your favorites and stacks between visits.
items.a7: Never. We don't sell or share your data, and we don't use advertising trackers. We only keep what's needed for the tool to work — see the Privacy page.
